Subject: Quick question on commit + burst fallback

Vivek — thanks again for the demo last week. The engineering team loved the latency profile; procurement raised a couple of contract questions before we proceed. Two quick ones we need to confirm so we can scope internal approvals:

1) Minimum monthly commit: do you support a soft-commit (crediting unused commit forward) or is it a hard spend floor?
2) Overage behavior: if we exceed committed tokens, do we pay on-demand overage rates immediately, or is there a burst bucket at a higher, temporary rate that auto-refunds if we drop back under the commit?

We'd like a short written description we can include in the SOW. Happy to hop on a 20 min call if that helps.

—Sanjay

Subject: Re: Quick question on commit + burst fallback

Thanks Sanjay — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then a recommended contractual phrasing below.

1) Minimum monthly commit: Redwood supports a firm monthly commit with a 3-month lookback option for new customers. Unused committed tokens are not auto-credited month-to-month in the base plan; instead, customers can convert unused committed spend into a one-time, non-refundable credit for Redwood add-ons (e.g., extended retention, Eval credits) within the quarter. For enterprise deals we can discuss a carry-forward credit structure — typically limited to one billing period.

2) Overage / burst handling: we offer a tiered fallback model:
  - Normal on-demand overage: charged at the agreed on-demand rate per token when sustained overage is observed beyond the commit for the billing period.
  - Burst buffer: short-lived traffic spikes under configured burst windows are served using a burst pool at a premium rate (typically 1.6x on-demand). If the monthly average remains under commit, we issue a post-billing credit equal to the delta between burst charges and committed unit economics (i.e., effectively refunding the premium for transient bursts).

Recommended SOW language (draft):
  "Customer will commit to a monthly token spend floor ("Commit"). Temporary exceedances within configured burst windows will be billed to a Burst Pool at the agreed burst rate. If, after monthly billing, Customer's total token consumption is less than or equal to the Commit, Redwood will issue a credit equal to the difference between Burst Pool charges and the Commit-equivalent rate for those tokens. Sustained usage above Commit will be billed at the on-demand overage rate stated in the Pricing Exhibit."

I've looped in Aditya for commercial terms and Monica for operational details (burst window sizing, throttling behavior). If that wording looks OK, we can hand it to your procurement/legal to include in the SOW.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on commit + burst fallback

Couple of operational clarifications from the infra/CS side to make sure the contractual language maps to behavior:

- Burst window definition: default is 5 minutes rolling for autoscaling into the burst pool. We can configure longer windows (up to 60 minutes) for a given route if CloudWave anticipates predictable spikes (e.g., batch jobs).
- Throttling vs queueing: when burst pool capacity is exhausted, requests are either queued (up to 2s) or served with graceful degradation (lower concurrency) depending on route policy. We recommend the queue option for critical user-facing endpoints to avoid 5xxs.
- Credit calculation: the post-billing credit only applies to tokens billed to the burst pool that are part of transient spikes. We calculate a daily moving average to identify transient vs sustained overage; sustained months are billed to on-demand rates and not eligible for refunds.

Attachment: Redwood_Overage_Playbook_v2.pdf — internal playbook that shows examples (spike A vs. spike B) and sample invoices. Sharing to help procurement + finance model costs.

If you want, we can add a clause that gives CloudWave an annual true-up review to convert unused commit into future credits (subject to mutual agreement).

—Monica
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
